title: Settings pages
description: Add a tab to the Settings section of the admin.

`/admin/settings` is a section with tabs. A layer adds a tab with a `settingsPages` entry and a page file.

## The tabs

`app/pages/admin/settings.vue` is the parent route. It shows the title, the tabs, a no-permission alert, and `<NuxtPage />`.

**General** is the first tab. It shows a language card and every registered `settingsPanels` entry. A settings driver stores the values.

The tabs show only when 2 or more pages are visible.

## Add a tab

Add a tab in two steps.

1. Make a page file at `app/pages/admin/settings/<x>.vue`. This is the route.
2. Register a `settingsPages` entry:

```ts [app/plugins/pluto-extension.ts]
definePlutoExtension({
  id: 'my-layer',
  settingsPages: [
    {
      id: 'reports',
      order: 30,
      label: 'my-layer.settings.reports',
      icon: 'lucide:chart-bar',
      to: '/admin/settings/reports',
      capability: 'reports:read'
    }
  ]
})
```

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | A key or a literal. |
| `icon` | Optional. |
| `to` | The route of the page. |
| `capability` | The capability that the user needs to see the tab. `'*'` means admin only. With no capability, every user in the admin sees the tab. |

Core registers two pages: `general` with order 0, and `email` with order 200. The `email` page is for administrators only (`capability: '*'`). See [Mail](/core/mail).

The page does not repeat the title. Core renders it.

## Check the capability on the server

The tab check is a UI convenience. The routes of your page must do their own server-side check.

## What else changes

- The sidebar **Settings** item gets one child for each visible page, when there are 2 or more pages.
- The command palette lists the pages in its "Go to" group. General shows once, as "Settings".

## `usePlutoSettingsPages()`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `all` | Every enabled page |
| `items` | The pages that the user may see, sorted by `order` |
| `current` | The page of the current route, by the longest `to` prefix |
| `allowed` | `false` when the current page needs a capability that the user lacks |

When `allowed` is false, the parent page shows a no-permission alert and not the child.

## Settings panels

A `settingsPanels` entry adds a form to the General tab. Register its component with `defineAsyncComponent`. The values go to the registered settings driver. A layer should namespace its setting keys, for example `blog.posts_per_page`, so that two layers never collide.

## Mail panels

A `mailPanels` entry adds a section to the Email settings page. See [Mail](/core/mail).
